h: Sharing the Holiness of Moshe on Shabbos

p: In the Shemoneh Esrei of Shabbos Shacharis
"Moshe rejoiced in the gift of his portion."
that it says in the holy Zohar
are called Shabbosos and Yamim Tovim."
of all the affairs of this world
and only occupy themselves with Torah
like the Shabbos day for Klal Yisrael,
from all the work of this world
And it also says in the holy Zohar
"The Shechinah did not depart from Yisrael
even in the Shabbosos of weekdays";
an allusion to what was said above:
of all the work of this world,
are sanctified with the holiness of Shabbos.
And the precision of the language in the holy Zohar,
that on Yom Tov it is permitted
to do work for preparing food,
which is not so on Shabbos;
and also the holiness of Shabbos
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
while Yom Tov is called "a holy convocation,"
And likewise there is a difference
among the souls of the talmidei chachamim too;
who are consecrated from their birth
כְּמוֹ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר יוֹחַאי וַחֲבֵירָיו
like Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and his colleagues,
and they were exempt from prayer,
and they did not turn their minds at all
to the needs of their livelihood;
and there was created for them
a carob tree and a spring of water.
as we have already spoken about this:
what they said in the Gemara (there):
do the will of the Omnipresent,
'And you shall gather in your grain'";
and the Maharsha asked in his Chiddushei Aggados:
"And it shall be, if you will diligently listen
"not doing the will of the Omnipresent"?
and the will of Hashem Yisbarach
for His service, may His Name be blessed;
and this is called "the will of the Omnipresent."
But the Holy One, blessed is He,
does not come with excessive demands upon His creatures;
לָזֶה לֹא צִוָּה בְּפֵירוּשׁ עַל זֶה
therefore He did not command this explicitly.
that when they came out of the cave
because they were leaving eternal life
and occupying themselves with temporal life,
"Have you come out to destroy My world?"
because the majority of the community
when they saw that old man
their minds were set at ease;
for they saw how beloved the mitzvos are
because this too is His commandment, may He be blessed,
of the mitzvah of resting on the Shabbos day;
they would have fulfilled His commandments as well
(and it was explained in Parashas Lech, section 3);
and to this the myrtle alludes,
for tzaddikim are likened to myrtles
for through the guarding of Shabbos
נִתְבָּרֵר שֶׁעַמֵּךְ כּוּלָּם צַדִּיקִים (יְשַׁעְיָה ס, כא)
it becomes clear that "your people are all tzaddikim" (Yeshayahu 60:21);
and people call it a myrtle."
Now there are also those souls
that are not suited for this
to dedicate most of their days
bread with salt you shall eat,
and water in measure you shall drink,"
and engage a little in work,
like Rabbi Yehoshua, who was a charcoal-maker,
barely, with just enough to live;
and it is a wholehearted service
from the side of an arousal from below,
And to this our Sages, of blessed memory, alluded
"And you shall serve Hashem your God"
which is the service of the heart;
"and He will bless your bread and your water"
which is the way of Torah;
"and I will remove illness from your midst."
is as they said, of blessed memory
"Why did they see fit to say 'Refa'einu' as the eighth?
Since circumcision was given on the eighth day,
therefore they fixed it as the eighth."
That is, the very essence of circumcision
is healing for the illness of the soul
which came about at the beginning of Creation
עַל יְדֵי הַפְּגָם שֶׁל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
through the blemish of Adam HaRishon,
which grew out of the corruption
at the end of the day
of the six days of Creation;
about which they said, of blessed memory
and through this it branched out in the offspring
with the screen of the foreskin
and for this healing and rectification are needed
until the time of the End;
"and He will heal the wound of His blow":
"He will heal the wound of the blow of the world."

"they whispered to it and it was calmed,"
"Before I formed you in the womb
And therefore he sold all that he had,

as he said to Rabbi Chiya bar Abba
Now regarding Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
it is known that the root of his soul was,
to be devoted to eternal life always
at the time of his birth (Shemos 2:2):
"And she saw him, that he was good";
the aspect of "the light, that it was good,"
in the passage of "Let there be light"
allude to the five books of the Torah
the whole house was filled with light;
of the people of his generation,
and their food was the man,
the bread that the ministering angels eat.
And it says in the holy Shelah
that you cannot read it this way
unless you read it that way;
on the tablet of their heart,
which is freedom from the Angel of Death
שֶׁהוּא הַלֵּב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ (קֹהֶלֶת י, ב)

Torah learning was implanted in their hearts"
on "the heart of a wise man at his right";
the yetzer hara was uprooted from their hearts"
from "the heart of a fool at his left."
And with this will be understood
what it says in the holy Zohar
to the giving of the Torah itself,
that the Torah was given on Shabbos";
and then were given the two Dibros,
which we heard from the mouth of the Almighty,
on the tablet of their heart;
and this is the meaning of
And then it was said to them (Shemos 19:6):
for they were prepared to be
only to His service, may His Name be blessed;
"And you shall be called the kohanim of Hashem."
And this is the matter of the holiness of Shabbos
in the essence of the soul,
that this is the root of the soul
of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
from the root of the Torah,
to be devoted to eternal life;
so that there not branch out from eating
anything from the aspect of the yetzer hara,
to those who ate the man;
enough for their livelihood without labor.
And with all that was said above we will understand
what we say on Shabbos Kodesh:
"Moshe rejoiced in the gift of his portion";
with the holiness of the soul
of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, in essence.
"For You called him a faithful servant,
he brought down in his hand,
and written in them is the guarding of Shabbos"
And on the Shabbos day itself
all the souls of Yisrael have
to the holiness of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
for they are free from all work
only to His service, may He be blessed,
for even the eating of Shabbos
is from the root of holiness,
that even the eating and drinking
as appears from its wording there;
